page.seo_title: Mody SEO: a free, simple SEO plugin for WordPress | Mody Cloud
page.seo_description: Mody SEO gives every page and post an SEO title and description in the editor's sidebar. Free (GPL), for single sites and multisites, no outside calls.
page.lead: Choose how each page and post shows in search results: an SEO title and an SEO description, written in the editor's sidebar.
page.problem_heading: Search results show what WordPress guesses
problem: Out of the box, WordPress makes each page's title from its name and your site's, and prints no description at all. Search engines then pick a snippet of the page themselves.
Larger SEO plugins add many screens, scores and settings. Mody SEO does one thing: it lets you write the two lines people read before they click.
page.features_heading: Two fields, in the place you already work

features.title: In the editor's sidebar
features.text: The Search engines panel sits in the document sidebar of the post editor and the Site Editor. Type an SEO title and an SEO description, see their length as you go, and save them with the page.

features.title: Sensible when empty
features.text: Leave a field empty and WordPress's own title is used ("Page title – Site"), and the page's excerpt becomes its description. The panel shows in grey what will be used.

features.title: One clean head
features.text: The SEO title becomes the page's whole title tag, and the description one meta description tag, cut at 160 characters at a word. Password-protected pages get no description.

features.title: Light on your database
features.text: Two post meta fields on pages, posts and the other public post types. No settings screen and no tables of its own. If WordPress's AI plugin is there, its own description gives way, so a page has one.

calls.title: Nothing while it works
calls.text: No outside service, no score computed elsewhere, no ping to search engines, no script or font from a CDN. Your titles and descriptions stay in your own database.

calls.title: mody.cloud, for updates
calls.text: At most twice a day it asks mody.cloud whether a newer version exists, so WordPress can show its usual update notice. The request carries nothing about your site: no address, no version.

calls.title: Where that request goes
calls.text: mody.cloud runs on our own server in Spain. While Mody Cloud is small, Cloudflare, a US company, sits in front of it and sees that request; we will replace it as soon as we can.

requirements: A single site or a multisite: activate it per site, or for the whole network
install: Download the zip from this page.
In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose the zip, then Install Now and Activate.
Open a page in the editor: the Search engines panel is in the sidebar.
page.mody_heading: Built into every Mody Cloud site
page.mody_text: On Mody Cloud, Mody SEO is already on, and Mody, your site's AI agent, writes the SEO title and description for you when you ask. Free: one site, no card, for people who live in Spain.

faq.q: Does it make a sitemap or add Open Graph tags?
faq.a: No. WordPress already makes a sitemap (wp-sitemap.xml). Mody SEO does not print Open Graph or Twitter tags yet, so link previews on social networks are left to WordPress and the network.

faq.q: Does it give my pages a score?
faq.a: No. There are no keyphrases, scores or traffic lights. Write the two lines for people: search results show about 60 characters of a title, and descriptions of 70 to 160 characters work best.

faq.q: What about categories, tags and archives?
faq.a: They keep WordPress's own title and get no description. Mody SEO covers pages, posts and the other public post types.

faq.q: Can I use it next to another SEO plugin?
faq.a: Better not: both would print a title and a description. Choose one.

faq.q: What happens if I remove it?
faq.a: Your pages keep their content. The two fields stay in the database and are simply no longer printed, so WordPress's own title comes back.

faq.q: Where do I report a problem or ask for help?
faq.a: Open an issue in our code repository on GitHub, with the link at the bottom of this page. We plan to move our code to Codeberg, a European home for open source.
